gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CNX Software's test of the 20 W Creality Falcon A1 Pro needed 7 passes at 85% power to cut 10 mm basswood, and the piece still didn't come loose. MakerWise reports Creality's rating as 10 mm in one pass. Two named reviewers also measured the 10 W Falcon A1 at about 75 dB while running.
standout_why: I read three cited rival pages. MakerWise says it did not test any machine hands-on and quotes only maker claims, such as Creality rating the A1 Pro at 10 mm basswood in one pass. Planet3DP lists only maker cut claims ('Each figure is the maker's own claim') and gives no dB figure. Tom's Hardware returned only its title to WebFetch, so I could not check what it measured. Among the other top results, EngraverPicker says it has not tested the machines, and CNCRouterInfo gives site scores and no measurements. Neither gives a dB figure or a reviewer cut test for the four machines ChatGPT picked. The xTool beginner guide and the xTool M2-vs-A1 page also returned only titles. No page I could read has a measured noise level or a measured cut result.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's 'more cutting power: Falcon A1 Pro' pick. In CNX's test, 10 mm basswood took 7 slow passes and still didn't fully cut through, so the shopper should expect several passes for thick wood rather than the rated single pass. Because the A1 measured about 75 dB on average and 80 dB at peak, the page should warn beginners that an enclosed machine is still loud enough to belong in a garage or separate room. For the xTool M2 pick, the only finding is a 3dwithus test showing the 10 W cuts 3 mm stock, about 16 minutes per box. Nothing I found shows it cutting thick wood or gives a dB figure.

findings.source_title: Creality Falcon A1: A Productive Consumer Laser? (3DPrint.com, 2025-06-12)

findings.label: 10 mm basswood cut test (CNX Software)
findings.value: 7 passes at 85% power, 600 mm/min; 10 min 15 s for the whole engrave-and-cut job; the piece did not fully separate
findings.source_title: Creality Falcon A1 Pro Review – An easy-to-use, fully enclosed 20W laser engraver with a built-in HD camera (Jean-Luc Aufranc, CNX Software, 2026-02-15, updated 2026-03-01)
findings.note: Air assist was on high. There was charring on the underside, and the piece had to be pried out by hand. MakerWise (https://maker-wise.com/articles/best-laser-engraver-for-beginners/, read 2026-11-10) attributes a one-pass 10 mm basswood rating to Creality. I could not open Creality's own page to confirm that rating (HTTP 429).

findings.source_title: Creality Falcon A1 Pro Review (CNX Software, 2026-02-15)
